match.reason: No point in the bank teaches the terms of trade; the balance of payments and net trade points are related but cover different ideas.

draft.title: The terms of trade
card: The terms of trade (TOT) compare the prices a country gets for its exports with the prices it pays for its imports. TOT = export price index ÷ import price index × 100.
If export prices rise faster than import prices, the TOT improve. If import prices rise faster than export prices, the TOT deteriorate.
When the TOT improve, the same quantity of exports buys more imports. Income earned from exports rises, so national income tends to rise.
Australia exports many commodities, such as iron ore and coal, so a rise in commodity prices tends to improve its TOT.
draft.remember: The terms of trade compare export prices with import prices. Higher export prices relative to import prices improve them.

a.q: Which change would improve Australia's terms of trade?
opts: Coal prices rise while import prices stay the same
Import prices rise while export prices stay the same
Iron ore prices fall while import prices stay the same
Import and export prices both fall by the same amount
a.why: The terms of trade compare export prices with import prices, so higher export prices with steady import prices improve them. Rising import prices do the opposite, even though they are also a price rise.
a.clue: Compare the price of what is sold with the price of what is bought.

b.q: In one year, Australia's export price index rises by 10% and its import price index rises by 15%. What happens to the terms of trade?
opts: They deteriorate, as import prices rose faster
They improve, as export prices rose
They stay the same, as both prices rose
They improve, as import prices rose more
b.why: Import prices rose faster than export prices, so the ratio of export prices to import prices falls and the terms of trade deteriorate. Export prices rising is not enough, because what matters is how they move compared with import prices.
b.clue: Which price index rose by more?

a.best: Coal prices rise while import prices stay the same

b.best: They deteriorate, as import prices rose faster

problems.detail: The option 'Import and export prices both fall by the same amount' is ambiguous. Read as the same percentage, the terms of trade are unchanged. Read as the same number of index points, the ratio changes whenever the two indexes start at different levels. Saying 'by the same percentage' would remove the doubt.
